description:
FILED s473t5c (#1501 round 4, `comp/` CHECK 2).  PRE-EXISTING.  SMALL (4 rows).

From perl 5.39.0 on, a version declaration imports the `builtin` functions of
that version's bundle into the lexical scope, exactly as it enables the
feature bundle -- so `use 5.39.0; my $t = true;` compiles and `$t eq "1"`.
Turning the version DOWN again does not remove them (`use builtin "true";
use v5.36; true` still works).  PCL enables the FEATURE bundle (#455 made the
region rule right) and does not import the builtins.

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):

    my $r = eval 'use 5.39.0; my $t = true; $t eq "1"';
    print "err=[$@] r=[", ($r//'undef'), "]\n";
    perl:  err=[] r=[1]
    PCL :  err=[Undefined subroutine &main::true called ...] r=[undef]

(The companion runner's sig for t/comp/use.t used to READ `undef-fn:main::pl-true`
for exactly this; it no longer does, because the surrounding eval now traps
it -- so the symptom moved from the file signature into the row.)

WHAT IT COSTS: t/comp/use.t rows 33-36 -- `builtin funcs available after
use 5.39.0`, `imported true is eq "1"` (x2), `builtin funcs not removed after
use v5.36`.  4 of the file's 47 fail rows.  The other 43 are #1689 (34, the
version REQUIREMENT check) and the strict-enforcement class (9,
not-supported.md §`use strict 'refs'` is not enforced / #1390).

LAYER: `builtin::` is the BLESSED shim-dispatch seam (DECIDED s377), so the
functions themselves are `lib/`-side and the missing piece is the parser's
bundle map -- the same table that maps `:5.NN` to a feature set should map it
to a builtin import set, keyed on the VERSION and never on a function name
(CLAUDE.md 9a's smell test: a literal `true` in `Pl/` would be the wrong
layer; the bundle DATA is language, like the pragma tables s408 blessed).
perl's own bundles: 5.39/5.40 give true false weaken unweaken is_weak blessed
refaddr reftype created_as_string created_as_number ceil floor
stringify trim indexed.
subject: A version bundle `use 5.39.0` / `use v5.40` does not import `builtin`'s `true`/`false`/`is_bool`... -- t/comp/use.t's 4 rows; the bundle-to-builtin map is missing where the feature map is present
